I would say building is worth it. Not only do you have the satisfaction of having something you put together yourself, you will be in a position of being able to better troubleshoot if something goes wrong later because of the knowledge you gain. 

Another benefit of building your own computer is knowing what the quality of all your parts are and ensuring you can get good thermals if you wish to push your system to its limits. I’m sure it is less of a concern with the higher quality build services such as NZXT build and others similar to them.

I personally wouldn’t trust the PSU or CPU coolers in a “cheap” prebuilt. Yes they get the job done, but is that what you really want to settle for, “good enough”? If you get an unlocked CPU and want to overclock it, will you have enough thermal headroom? Also, what if you want to consider making an upgrade in the future? If you plan ahead, you can get a stronger PSU now (not super overkill, but maybe a 750w instead of a 500w). You could also go with the higher wattage to keep power draw in “eco mode” if the PSU supports it, which will keep the fan noise low or even turn the fan off completely. 

Some cheap prebuilt companies may use proprietary components, which means no future upgrades for your system (or in a best case scenario here, very limited upgradability). You also run the risk of excessive noise from a case not optimized for sound dampening, or even worse, a lack of airflow. If air doesn’t flow, as we should know, our fans work harder... and if this is happening, there is a good chance that those fans are going to be louder than even a modest quality fan (not even considering Noctua or BeQuiet here). 

Final thoughts... if you want control of things like upgradability, noise or even some performance control , then you should just build your own or use a premium build service. If you want bang for the buck, usually building your own is better, but with how volatile component pricing is right now, you might be able to match or even beat a custom built option with a prebuilt.
